components.label: Report API
components.responsibility: Authenticate a user, validate parameters and generate a bounded report within one request lifecycle.

components.label: Access check
components.responsibility: Authenticate the principal and require request.ownerId to equal it before reading any receipt; receipts are keyed by (ownerId, requestKey), so a read can only return the caller's own receipt.

components.label: Request receipt store
components.responsibility: One transaction inserts or reads the receipt for (ownerId, requestKey) with parameter hash, report ID, source cutoff, running status, attempt token and deadline. A retry during a live attempt returns running; after the deadline it gets the next token and keeps the stored cutoff.

components.label: Source snapshot reader
components.responsibility: Read source rows at the snapshot cutoff stored in the receipt when it was first accepted, never one chosen per attempt, so every attempt renders the same inputs.

components.label: Bounded renderer
components.responsibility: Enforce row, byte and work budgets; abort with explicit failure before publishing an incomplete artifact.

components.label: Immutable artifact store
components.responsibility: Store bytes under hash-addressed identity and bind output hash to the report; repeated identical writes are harmless.

components.label: Completion commit
components.responsibility: Commit metadata by compare-and-set from running to complete, only for an issued attempt token and a verified artifact hash. A later completion gets the committed receipt back and its bytes become an orphan to reconcile; a failed commit leaves the receipt running until its deadline.

components.label: Failure and load observations
components.responsibility: For this hypothetical design record request duration, timeouts, CPU work and database wait as proposed measurements. A tenfold input is a scenario, not observed capacity.

components.label: Illustrative report user
components.responsibility: Invoke the documented API and retain returned outcomes.

components.label: Job submission API
components.responsibility: Persist a report job and dispatch intent atomically, return accepted, and let a leased worker publish completion later.

components.label: Job and request ledger
components.responsibility: Atomically create unique owner/requestKey receipt, parameter hash and job record; conflicting payloads reject.

components.label: Transactional dispatch outbox
components.responsibility: Commit outbox row with the job in the same database transaction; a dispatcher retries delivery by job ID.

components.label: Fenced worker claim
components.responsibility: Claim in one transaction only when the job is accepted or its current lease has expired: raise the fencing token, record the worker and a new deadline. Reject claims on complete jobs and on unexpired leases; completion verifies the current token.

components.label: Snapshot report worker
components.responsibility: Pin query cutoff and renderer version in the job before work; retries reuse them or explicitly create a new report version. Worker count and lease length are the knobs an illustrative tenfold scenario would measure through queue age and worker utilization.

components.label: Immutable output repository
components.responsibility: Write immutable content by hash; completion records one authorized artifact choice under the current fencing token.

components.label: Versioned status API
components.responsibility: Authorize each read and report accepted/running/complete/failed/uncertain; complete requires verified artifact and fenced metadata commit. Progress percentages, if used, are measured work or omitted.

components.label: Lease and artifact reconciler
components.responsibility: Scan unfinished jobs and artifacts, verify identity/hash, requeue or reconcile with a fresh lease. Unknown irreversible effects stay uncertain.

problem.scope: Explicitly illustrative worked examples, not the user's project, employment history or a claimed incident. Review a hypothetical report-generation product as two alternative designs: synchronous transactional requests and asynchronous durable jobs. All traffic, failures and scaling questions below are authored scenarios. Replace them with verified project facts before using as personal experience; no actual operated scale or business outcome is asserted.

evidence.testName: batch-08 review synchronous: owner-scoped receipts, stored cutoff and first completion

acceptanceCases.given: Illustrative request K from owner A is accepted and its response lost; owner B presents the same key K.
acceptanceCases.then: A's identical retry returns the same report ID; conflicting reuse returns 409 without new work; B gets its own receipt and never A's report; B acting as A is forbidden.
acceptanceCases.when: A retries K with identical parameters, then reuses K with different parameters; B submits K, and B claims to be A.

evidence.testName: batch-08 review synchronous: owner-scoped receipts, stored cutoff and first completion

acceptanceCases.given: Illustrative retries of K overlap: a second arrives while the first attempt is running and a third after the first attempt's deadline.
acceptanceCases.then: The second retry renders nothing and returns running; the third takes attempt token 2 but renders from the cutoff stored at first acceptance; the first completion commits and the later one returns the committed receipt unchanged.
acceptanceCases.when: Both rendering attempts finish, the first one first.

evidence.testName: batch-08 review synchronous: owner-scoped receipts, stored cutoff and first completion

acceptanceCases.given: A hypothetical attempt whose artifact write succeeds but whose completion is lost or reports a mismatched hash.
acceptanceCases.then: The mismatched completion is rejected and the receipt stays running; the retry keeps the report ID and stored cutoff and completes once; a completion for an attempt never issued is rejected. No personal incident claim is made.
acceptanceCases.when: Complete with the mismatched hash, retry after the attempt deadline, and complete with verified bytes.

acceptanceCases.given: An illustrative report whose rows or bytes exceed the declared request budget.
acceptanceCases.then: The attempt aborts before any artifact write and the receipt records failed; no partial byte stream is presented as complete.

acceptanceCases.given: An illustrative tenfold arrival scenario for this hypothetical product.
acceptanceCases.then: The plan names the measurements needed (request duration, timeouts, CPU work, database wait) and the evidence that would justify durable jobs; no throughput number, incident or outcome is asserted.
acceptanceCases.when: Plan how to decide whether to keep synchronous requests.

guarantees: Retry intent is owner-scoped; one attempt is live at a time; all attempts read one stored cutoff; the first completion wins.

solutions.chooseWhen: Reports are small enough for a declared bounded request deadline and simplicity matters.

stages.explanation: Authenticate a user, validate parameters and generate a bounded report within one request lifecycle. This illustrative path returns a finished report or an explicit running, failed or uncertain status in one request; it is not a claim about a real project. [An API contract](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Application_programming_interface) states what callers send, what an outcome means, and how failures are reported. It should remain clear before the implementation is split into more components.

stages.question: Which user action is being traced?
stages.reason: Authenticate a user, validate parameters and generate a bounded report within one request lifecycle.
stages.title: Expose Report API

stages.explanation: Authenticate the principal and require request.ownerId to equal it before reading any receipt; receipts are keyed by (ownerId, requestKey), so a read can only return the caller's own receipt. Idempotency lookup never bypasses authorization. [Access control](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Access_control) decides whether an authenticated identity may perform a particular action. The check must apply to the actual resource and operation, including cached and asynchronous paths.
stages.question: May a caller read another owner's report?
stages.reason: Authenticate the principal and require request.ownerId to equal it before reading any receipt; receipts are keyed by (ownerId, requestKey), so a read can only return the caller's own receipt.
stages.title: Authorize report ownership

stages.explanation: One transaction inserts or reads the receipt for (ownerId, requestKey) with parameter hash, report ID, source cutoff, running status, attempt token and deadline. A retry during a live attempt returns running; after the deadline it gets the next token and keeps the stored cutoff. At most one attempt per receipt is live; reused keys with different parameters conflict. [Backoff](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Exponential_backoff) spaces repeated attempts so failures do not create a burst of extra traffic.
invariants: At most one attempt per receipt is live; reused keys with different parameters conflict.
stages.question: What if the response is lost?
stages.reason: One transaction inserts or reads the receipt for (ownerId, requestKey) with parameter hash, report ID, source cutoff, running status, attempt token and deadline. A retry during a live attempt returns running; after the deadline it gets the next token and keeps the stored cutoff.
stages.title: Persist retry intent

stages.explanation: Read source rows at the snapshot cutoff stored in the receipt when it was first accepted, never one chosen per attempt, so every attempt renders the same inputs. Every attempt of one receipt reads the same stored cutoff. [A snapshot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Snapshot_isolation) gives one read operation a fixed view of data. Later writes may change the live system without changing the rows that reader sees.
invariants: Every attempt of one receipt reads the same stored cutoff.
stages.question: Can a running query mix source versions?
stages.reason: Read source rows at the snapshot cutoff stored in the receipt when it was first accepted, never one chosen per attempt, so every attempt renders the same inputs.
stages.title: Freeze report inputs

stages.explanation: Enforce row, byte and work budgets; abort with explicit failure before publishing an incomplete artifact. A partial byte stream is never advertised as complete. [A race condition](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Race_condition) makes an outcome depend on which operation finishes first. Responses need an identity or generation check so an older request cannot overwrite newer user intent.
invariants: A partial byte stream is never advertised as complete.
stages.question: What if the report exceeds the request budget?
stages.reason: Enforce row, byte and work budgets; abort with explicit failure before publishing an incomplete artifact.
stages.title: Generate within deadline

stages.explanation: Store bytes under hash-addressed identity and bind output hash to the report; repeated identical writes are harmless. A completed receipt references immutable matching content. [Immutable data](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Immutable_object) is built as a complete new value rather than changed underneath readers. Publishing one reference lets each reader keep a consistent version. Consider this case: A hypothetical attempt whose artifact write succeeds but whose completion is lost or reports a mismatched hash.
invariants: A completed receipt references immutable matching content.
stages.question: Can retry overwrite a completed report?
stages.reason: Store bytes under hash-addressed identity and bind output hash to the report; repeated identical writes are harmless.
stages.title: Publish named output

stages.explanation: Commit metadata by compare-and-set from running to complete, only for an issued attempt token and a verified artifact hash. A later completion gets the committed receipt back and its bytes become an orphan to reconcile; a failed commit leaves the receipt running until its deadline. The first verified completion wins; the artifact write and metadata commit are not called atomic. [Transaction guarantees](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ACID) describe which changes become visible together and what survives failure.
invariants: The first verified completion wins; the artifact write and metadata commit are not called atomic.
stages.question: Are object storage and database commit one transaction?
stages.reason: Commit metadata by compare-and-set from running to complete, only for an issued attempt token and a verified artifact hash. A later completion gets the committed receipt back and its bytes become an orphan to reconcile; a failed commit leaves the receipt running until its deadline.
stages.title: Let the first completion win

stages.explanation: For this hypothetical design record request duration, timeouts, CPU work and database wait as proposed measurements. A tenfold input is a scenario, not observed capacity. No actual incident, throughput or user outcome is invented. [Transaction guarantees](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ACID) describe which changes become visible together and what survives failure. They must be tied to explicit storage behavior rather than inferred from a successful API call.
invariants: No actual incident, throughput or user outcome is invented.

evidence.testName: batch-08 review durable-jobs: job identity, lease-checked claims and fenced completion

acceptanceCases.given: Illustrative request K is accepted and its response lost; another owner reads the job and submits its own K.
acceptanceCases.then: The same report ID and a single outbox row are reused; conflicting reuse is rejected without a new job; the other owner's read is forbidden and its own K creates a separate job.
acceptanceCases.when: Retry K with identical parameters, then reuse K with different parameters.

evidence.testName: batch-08 review durable-jobs: job identity, lease-checked claims and fenced completion

acceptanceCases.given: A hypothetical job claimed by worker 1 with a 10-unit lease.
acceptanceCases.then: The claim at 5 is rejected while the lease is live; the claim at 11 raises the fence; worker 1's late completion is rejected as stale; the claim after completion is rejected.
acceptanceCases.when: Worker 2 claims at time 5 and again at time 11; worker 1 then tries to complete; a third claim arrives after completion.

evidence.testName: batch-08 review durable-jobs: job identity, lease-checked claims and fenced completion

acceptanceCases.given: A hypothetical worker writes an artifact and its metadata acknowledgement is lost.
acceptanceCases.then: Corrupt bytes are rejected and the job stays running; verified bytes complete it under the current fence; a retry of K returns the completed artifact. No personal incident claim is made.
acceptanceCases.when: Resume under a fresh lease and complete with the job's current token, first with corrupt bytes and then with verified bytes.

acceptanceCases.given: The same illustrative tenfold arrival scenario.
acceptanceCases.then: The plan names queue age, worker utilization and lease expiry rate as proposed measurements under a declared workload; no capacity number or production result is asserted.
acceptanceCases.when: Plan how to size workers and leases.

guarantees: Durable intent precedes dispatch; a claim needs an accepted job or an expired lease; only the current lease holder can commit completion.

stages.explanation: Atomically create unique owner/requestKey receipt, parameter hash and job record; conflicting payloads reject. Identical retries reuse report ID. [Transaction guarantees](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ACID) describe which changes become visible together and what survives failure. They must be tied to explicit storage behavior rather than inferred from a successful API call. They must be tied to explicit storage behavior rather than inferred from a successful API call.

stages.question: What if enqueue fails after job commit?
stages.reason: Commit outbox row with the job in the same database transaction; a dispatcher retries delivery by job ID.

stages.explanation: Claim in one transaction only when the job is accepted or its current lease has expired: raise the fencing token, record the worker and a new deadline. Reject claims on complete jobs and on unexpired leases; completion verifies the current token. A claim never raises the fence while a live lease exists, and lease expiry alone never lets a stale token commit. [Fencing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fencing_%28computing%29) prevents an outdated owner from continuing to modify shared resources.
invariants: A claim never raises the fence while a live lease exists, and lease expiry alone never lets a stale token commit.
stages.question: Can an expired worker publish stale completion?
stages.reason: Claim in one transaction only when the job is accepted or its current lease has expired: raise the fencing token, record the worker and a new deadline. Reject claims on complete jobs and on unexpired leases; completion verifies the current token.
stages.title: Recover worker loss

stages.explanation: Pin query cutoff and renderer version in the job before work; retries reuse them or explicitly create a new report version. Worker count and lease length are the knobs an illustrative tenfold scenario would measure through queue age and worker utilization. One job ID does not silently change input semantics. [Backoff](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Exponential_backoff) spaces repeated attempts so failures do not create a burst of extra traffic.
invariants: One job ID does not silently change input semantics.
stages.question: Does a retry read different source data?
stages.reason: Pin query cutoff and renderer version in the job before work; retries reuse them or explicitly create a new report version. Worker count and lease length are the knobs an illustrative tenfold scenario would measure through queue age and worker utilization.
stages.title: Compute from pinned inputs

stages.explanation: Write immutable content by hash; completion records one authorized artifact choice under the current fencing token. Remote writes may duplicate, but stale workers cannot replace committed metadata. [Immutable data](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Immutable_object) is built as a complete new value rather than changed underneath readers. Publishing one reference lets each reader keep a consistent version.
invariants: Remote writes may duplicate, but stale workers cannot replace committed metadata.
stages.question: What if duplicate workers render the same job?
stages.reason: Write immutable content by hash; completion records one authorized artifact choice under the current fencing token.
stages.title: Store complete artifacts

stages.explanation: Authorize each read and report accepted/running/complete/failed/uncertain; complete requires verified artifact and fenced metadata commit. Progress percentages, if used, are measured work or omitted. Every status read is authorized for its owner and changes no job state. [Transaction guarantees](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ACID) describe which changes become visible together and what survives failure. They must be tied to explicit storage behavior rather than inferred from a successful API call.
invariants: Every status read is authorized for its owner and changes no job state.
stages.question: Can polling report complete before bytes exist?
stages.reason: Authorize each read and report accepted/running/complete/failed/uncertain; complete requires verified artifact and fenced metadata commit. Progress percentages, if used, are measured work or omitted.
stages.title: Expose progress honestly

stages.explanation: Scan unfinished jobs and artifacts, verify identity/hash, requeue or reconcile with a fresh lease. Unknown irreversible effects stay uncertain. Recovery does not claim an incident actually occurred or prove deployed reliability. [Fencing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fencing_%28computing%29) prevents an outdated owner from continuing to modify shared resources. A newer owner needs a token that the resource checks, not merely a belief that ownership changed.
invariants: Recovery does not claim an incident actually occurred or prove deployed reliability.

stages.reason: Scan unfinished jobs and artifacts, verify identity/hash, requeue or reconcile with a fresh lease. Unknown irreversible effects stay uncertain.
